Legal damage means the violation of a legal right, not necessarily actual loss.

items.stem: "Opening a rival school that reduces another school's income is not a tort." Examine this statement with reference to meaning and essentials of a tort.
items.answer: The statement is valid. It causes loss without violating any legal right (damnum sine injuria).
items.markingKey: 3 marks: 1 for accepting or qualifying the statement, 1 for the reason (it causes loss without violating any legal right (damnum sine injuria).), 1 for supporting evidence from the chapter.

items.stem:
Study the extract below and answer the questions.
"The same act may be both a tort and a crime, such as assault. The essentials of a tort are a wrongful act or omission, legal damage and a legal remedy. Legal damage means the violation of a legal right, not necessarily actual loss. In a crime the offender is punished, while in a tort the injured person is compensated."
(i) Explain the term 'injuria sine damno', which is related to the theme of the extract. (1)
(ii) Using the extract and your own knowledge, explain the following: Opening a rival school that reduces another school's income is not a tort. (1)
(iii) A student concludes: "A tort is a public wrong prosecuted by the State." Use your knowledge of the chapter to evaluate this conclusion. (2)
items.answer: (i) The violation of a legal right without actual loss, which is actionable. (ii) It causes loss without violating any legal right (damnum sine injuria). (iii) The conclusion is wrong: A tort is a private civil wrong; a crime is a public wrong.
items.markingKey: 1+1+2 marks: (i) The violation of a legal right without actual loss, which is actionable. (ii) It causes loss without violating any legal right (damnum sine injuria). (iii) The conclusion is wrong: A tort is a private civil wrong; a crime is a public wrong.

items.stem: What is meant by 'tort' in the context of meaning and essentials of a tort?
items.answer: A civil wrong, other than a breach of contract, for which the remedy is an action for unliquidated damages.

items.markingKey: 1 mark for the corrected statement (Knowledge is not consent; the person must voluntarily agree to the risk.); 1 mark for a supporting fact from the CBSE textbook chapter.

items.stem: Which one of the following statements about vicarious liability, nuisance and defamation is correct?
items.answer: For defamation the statement must refer to the plaintiff and be published to a third person.
items.markingKey: (d) The others are wrong: It must be published to a third person. Slander is transient; libel is permanent. Liability arises only for acts in the course of employment.
options: A statement made only to the person defamed is defamation.
Slander is defamation in a permanent form.
An employer is liable for every act of an employee, even outside work.
For defamation the statement must refer to the plaintiff and be published to a third person.

items.stem: "Wrongfully refusing a voter the right to vote is a tort." Examine this statement with reference to meaning and essentials of a tort.
items.answer: The statement is valid. The violation of a legal right is actionable even without actual loss.
items.markingKey: 3 marks: 1 for accepting or qualifying the statement, 1 for the reason (the violation of a legal right is actionable even without actual loss.), 1 for supporting evidence from the chapter.

items.stem: The following statement about negligence; strict and absolute liability is incorrect. Rewrite it correctly and justify your correction: "Negligence requires an intention to cause harm."
items.answer: Negligence is careless conduct; no intention is needed.
items.markingKey: 1 mark for the corrected statement (Negligence is careless conduct; no intention is needed.); 1 mark for a supporting fact from the CBSE textbook chapter.

items.stem: Which one of the following statements about vicarious liability, nuisance and defamation is NOT correct?
items.answer: An employer is liable for every act of an employee, even outside work.
items.markingKey: (b) It is incorrect. Liability arises only for acts in the course of employment.
options: For defamation the statement must refer to the plaintiff and be published to a third person.
An employer is liable for every act of an employee, even outside work.
Nuisance may be public, affecting the public at large, or private, affecting particular persons.
An employer is liable only for torts committed by an employee in the course of employment.

items.stem:
Assertion (A): A manufacturer may be liable to a consumer with whom it has no contract.
Reason (R): Vicarious liability arises in relationships such as master and servant, principal and agent, and partners.
Choose the correct option.
items.answer: Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
items.markingKey: (b) Both statements are true, but R deals with a different point and does not explain A.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.

items.stem: In the study of general defences in torts, the term 'private defence' refers to:
items.answer: The defence that reasonable force was used to protect one's person or property
items.markingKey: (a) 'private defence' means the defence that reasonable force was used to protect one's person or property.
options: The defence that reasonable force was used to protect one's person or property
The rule in M.C. Mehta v Union of India that an enterprise engaged in a hazardous activity is liable for harm without any exceptions
Defamation in a transient form, such as spoken words or gestures
The defence that harm was caused by natural forces so extraordinary that they could not be foreseen or guarded against

items.stem: Which one of the following statements about meaning and essentials of a tort is NOT correct?
items.answer: A tort is a public wrong prosecuted by the State.
items.markingKey: (a) It is incorrect. A tort is a private civil wrong; a crime is a public wrong.
options: A tort is a public wrong prosecuted by the State.
In tort the duty is fixed by law, while in contract the duty is fixed by the parties.
In a crime the offender is punished, while in a tort the injured person is compensated.
The essentials of a tort are a wrongful act or omission, legal damage and a legal remedy.

items.stem:
Read the following extract on negligence; strict and absolute liability and answer the questions that follow.
"The absolute liability rule was evolved after the Bhopal gas tragedy and the Oleum gas leak. Exceptions to strict liability include the plaintiff's own default, act of God, consent, act of a third party and statutory authority. Under res ipsa loquitur the burden shifts to the defendant to show that there was no negligence."
(i) The rule of absolute liability was laid down in: (1)
(ii) Explain the term 'res ipsa loquitur' as it relates to this theme. (1)
(iii) Explain the reason behind the following: A surgeon who leaves a swab inside a patient is presumed negligent. (2)
items.answer: (i) M.C. Mehta v Union of India (Oleum gas leak case) (ii) The principle that 'the thing speaks for itself', under which negligence is presumed from the nature of the accident. (iii) Under res ipsa loquitur the facts speak for themselves.
items.markingKey: 1+1+2 marks: (i) M.C. Mehta v Union of India (Oleum gas leak case) (ii) The principle that 'the thing speaks for itself', under which negligence is presumed from the nature of the accident. (iii) Under res ipsa loquitur the facts speak for themselves.

items.stem:
Assertion (A): Necessity is a valid defence.
Reason (R): The harm was caused to prevent a greater harm to the public.
Choose the correct option.
items.answer: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
items.markingKey: (a) Both are true and R explains A: the harm was caused to prevent a greater harm to the public.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.

items.stem:
Consider the following statements about vicarious liability, nuisance and defamation:
I. A statement made only to the person defamed is defamation.
II. An employer is liable for every act of an employee, even outside work.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
items.answer: Neither I nor II
items.markingKey: (d) I is incorrect: It must be published to a third person. II is incorrect: Liability arises only for acts in the course of employment.
options: I only
II only
Both I and II
Neither I nor II

items.stem:
Read the following statements about meaning and essentials of a tort:
I. Legal damage means the violation of a legal right, not necessarily actual loss.
II. The same act may be both a tort and a crime, such as assault.
III. The essentials of a tort are a wrongful act or omission, legal damage and a legal remedy.
Which of these statements are correct?
items.answer: All of them
items.markingKey: (b) I is correct. II is correct. III is correct.
options: I and III only
All of them
III only
II and III only

items.stem:
Study the extract below and answer the questions.
"Under res ipsa loquitur the burden shifts to the defendant to show that there was no negligence. Under absolute liability, compensation is linked to the magnitude and capacity of the enterprise. Exceptions to strict liability include the plaintiff's own default, act of God, consent, act of a third party and statutory authority. The absolute liability rule was evolved after the Bhopal gas tragedy and the Oleum gas leak."
(i) Explain the term 'duty of care', which is related to the theme of the extract. (1)
(ii) Using the extract and your own knowledge, explain the following: A surgeon who leaves a swab inside a patient is presumed negligent. (1)
(iii) A student concludes: "Strict liability was laid down in M.C. Mehta v Union of India." Use your knowledge of the chapter to evaluate this conclusion. (2)
items.answer: (i) The legal obligation to take reasonable care to avoid acts that could foreseeably harm others. (ii) Under res ipsa loquitur the facts speak for themselves. (iii) The conclusion is wrong: It was laid down in Rylands v Fletcher; M.C. Mehta laid down absolute liability.
items.markingKey: 1+1+2 marks: (i) The legal obligation to take reasonable care to avoid acts that could foreseeably harm others. (ii) Under res ipsa loquitur the facts speak for themselves. (iii) The conclusion is wrong: It was laid down in Rylands v Fletcher; M.C. Mehta laid down absolute liability.

items.stem: Which one of the following statements about general defences in torts is NOT correct?
items.answer: An inevitable accident must involve natural forces.
items.markingKey: (c) It is incorrect. That is an act of God; an inevitable accident need not involve natural forces.
options: In private defence the force used must be reasonable and proportionate.
Consent under volenti non fit injuria must be free and given with knowledge of the risk.
An inevitable accident must involve natural forces.
An act of God involves natural forces and an event that could not reasonably be anticipated.

items.stem:
Assertion (A): An employer is liable for every act of an employee, even outside work.
Reason (R): For defamation the statement must refer to the plaintiff and be published to a third person.
Choose the correct option.
items.answer: A is false, but R is true.
items.markingKey: (d) A is false: Liability arises only for acts in the course of employment. R is true.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.

items.stem: Which term describes the following? The principle that 'the thing speaks for itself', under which negligence is presumed from the nature of the accident.
items.answer: res ipsa loquitur
items.markingKey: (a) res ipsa loquitur: the principle that 'the thing speaks for itself', under which negligence is presumed from the nature of the accident.
options: res ipsa loquitur
damnum sine injuria
tort
crime

items.stem:
Read the following extract on meaning and essentials of a tort and answer the questions that follow.
"In a crime the offender is punished, while in a tort the injured person is compensated. The same act may be both a tort and a crime, such as assault. The essentials of a tort are a wrongful act or omission, legal damage and a legal remedy."
(i) The remedy in tort is mainly: (1)
(ii) Explain the term 'damnum sine injuria' as it relates to this theme. (1)
(iii) Explain the reason behind the following: Opening a rival school that reduces another school's income is not a tort. (2)
items.answer: (i) unliquidated damages (ii) Actual loss without the violation of a legal right, which is not actionable. (iii) It causes loss without violating any legal right (damnum sine injuria).
items.markingKey: 1+1+2 marks: (i) unliquidated damages (ii) Actual loss without the violation of a legal right, which is not actionable. (iii) It causes loss without violating any legal right (damnum sine injuria).

items.stem: Which one of the following statements about general defences in torts is correct?
items.answer: Consent under volenti non fit injuria must be free and given with knowledge of the risk.
items.markingKey: (b) The others are wrong: Rescue cases are an exception to the defence. Knowledge is not consent; the person must voluntarily agree to the risk. That is an act of God; an inevitable accident need not involve natural forces.
options: Volenti non fit injuria protects a defendant in rescue cases.
Consent under volenti non fit injuria must be free and given with knowledge of the risk.
An inevitable accident must involve natural forces.
Mere knowledge of a risk always amounts to consent.

items.stem:
Statement: An employer is made liable for an employee's tort.
Which one of the following best explains this statement?
items.answer: The employer controls the work and is better able to pay compensation.
items.markingKey: (b) The employer controls the work and is better able to pay compensation.
options: Public nuisance affects the public generally and is a matter for the State.
The employer controls the work and is better able to pay compensation.
It causes loss without violating any legal right (damnum sine injuria).
Defamation protects only a reputation that is deserved.
